samasa.literal: those whose minds are filled with joy

morph.note: Perfect plural of √भू: ‘(they) became’, with the predicate हर्षनिर्भरमानसाः.
Perfect plural of √गै: the root takes the form गा in the perfect (ज-गुः, with the reduplicated g → j).
Here an adverb, ‘sweetly’ (as in 7.26, ललितं … वचः); it is not a name.

mantras.anvaya: ततः तस्मिन् निहते सर्वे देवगणाः हर्षनिर्भरमानसाः बभूवुः। गन्धर्वाः ललितं जगुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: A locative absolute (निहते तस्मिन्) between two clauses: देवगणाः … हर्षनिर्भरमानसाः बभूवुः, and गन्धर्वाः ललितं जगुः.
mantras.lit: Then, he having been slain, all the hosts of gods became those whose minds are filled with joy; the gandharvas sang sweetly.
mantras.tr: Then, with Śumbha slain, all the hosts of the gods were filled with joy, and the gandharvas sang sweetly.

comm.t: The celebration begins. The scene repeats the rejoicing after Mahiṣa’s death (3.44: जगुर्गन्धर्वपतयो ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः), as the end of each great battle is marked by music and dance.
A modern reading: the gods have not fought this last battle; they have only watched (10.10). Their joy is the joy of those who are saved by another.

mantras.anvaya: तथा एव अन्ये अवादयन्, अप्सरोगणाः च ननृतुः। तथा पुण्याः वाताः ववुः। दिवाकरः सुप्रभः अभूत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four short clauses joined by तथा and च: others played, the apsarases danced, the winds blew, the sun became bright.
mantras.lit: Likewise others played (instruments), and the troops of apsarases danced. Likewise pure winds blew; the sun became of fair radiance.
mantras.tr: Others played music, the apsarases danced, pure winds blew, and the sun shone brightly.

comm.t: The joy of heaven is matched by the healing of nature: music and dance among the gods, pure winds and a clear sun in the world.
A modern reading: the verse joins two orders of response — the arts of the celestials and the weather of the earth. Liberation is shown as both festivity and the return of ordinary health.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya containing a saptamī tatpuruṣa (दिग्जनित = दिक्षु जनितः)
samasa.sense: the ominous noises that had been heard from every direction
samasa.alt: Also pañcamī tatpuruṣa in the first member, दिग्भ्यः जनिताः, ‘produced from the quarters’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: The same participle twice, in two functions. The first qualifies अग्नयः: the fires blazed ‘calm’ — burning steadily rather than flaring (alt.: ‘the fires that had been quenched blazed up again’, शान्ताः then meaning ‘extinguished’). The second is the predicate of the next clause: ‘stilled (were) the sounds’.

mantras.anvaya: अग्नयः च शान्ताः जज्वलुः। दिग्जनितस्वनाः शान्ताः (अभवन्)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses: अग्नयः (with शान्ताः) जज्वलुः, and दिग्जनितस्वनाः शान्ताः with the verb ‘were’ understood.
mantras.lit: And the fires blazed, calm; stilled (were) the sounds arisen in the quarters.
mantras.tr: The fires blazed up, steady and calm, and the noises that had sounded from every quarter fell still.
mantras.tr_note: The first शान्ताः is rendered ‘steady and calm’; ‘were’ is supplied in the second clause.

comm.t: The last half-śloka of the chapter completes the restoration: fire and sound, which had been disturbed, return to their proper state. The first शान्ताः can also be read ‘(the fires) that had been put out (blazed again)’ — on either reading the fires are restored. This half-line is the one ‘half-śloka’ of the chapter’s colophon count (27 ślokas and 1 half-śloka).

The fires are traditionally understood as the sacrificial fires. Śumbha had claimed every share of the sacrifice for himself (5.108, यज्ञभागानहं सर्वानुपाश्नामि); with him gone, the fires burn again for the gods. The verse itself says only ‘the fires’. In recitation the chapter ends with the bīja ॐ, which belongs to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa.

flags.uncertain: Interpretation, not reading: the first शान्ताः may describe the fires as calm (steady) or as having been extinguished before they blazed again. The first is taken here.
